- **pictorial form (*Form der Abbildung*)** against **logical form (*logische Form*)** — the 2022 question in five words
- **projective relation** — the method of projection that makes a propositional sign into a proposition
- **shown, not said** — the closing move of the session, developed fully in Session 11

**How to use them:** 2022 Q3(c) asks a two-part question — is there a difference between pictorial and logical form, and how does logical form define the relation between language and reality? #### 1. Why the world is facts and not things ✅

- ✅ **The argument.** A complete inventory of objects leaves everything undecided: it does not tell you which qualities they have or how they are related. What is the case is a matter of **configuration**, and a configuration is a fact. Hence 1.1.
- ✅ **Objects and their possibilities.** An object is characterised not by an intrinsic description but by the **states of affairs into which it can enter** (2.0121, 2.013). Possibility is written into the object; the space of possible configurations is fixed once the objects are fixed.
- ⚠️ **The honest gap.** Wittgenstein gives **no uncontested example** of a simple object or an elementary proposition. The text argues that simples are *required* — determinate sense demands a final base — rather than exhibiting them. ⚠️ Say this explicitly; it is a standing criticism, and pre-empting it earns the assessment mark.
- ⚠️ **The contrast with Russell.** Russell's atoms are identified epistemically, through acquaintance, in the 1918 phase. Wittgenstein's objects are postulated by a **condition-of-sense argument** and are never identified. Two atomisms, one word.

#### 2. What "picture" does and does not mean ✅

- ✅ **It is a technical notion.** A picture is anything that shares form with what it represents and whose elements are correlated with elements of the represented situation. Resemblance in the everyday sense is **irrelevant**; a musical score does not look like music.
- ✅ **The propositional sign and the method of projection.** A written or spoken sentence is a **propositional sign** — a fact in its own right, since its elements stand in a determinate relation. The sign together with its **projective relation** to the world is the **proposition** (3.11–3.12). Meaning is not a mental accompaniment; it is a projection.
- ⚠️ **Provenance discipline.** The label "picture theory" is the **commentators'**. Wittgenstein writes of *Bild* — picture or model — and of *abbilden*, to depict. Write "the doctrine usually called the picture theory" once, and the provenance mark is secured.
- ⚠️ **What the theory explains that a name-theory cannot.** How a sentence can be understood before you know whether it is true. On a naming model, an understood sentence would need an existing object to correspond to it; on the picturing model it needs only a **possible** configuration. That is why falsity is not a failure of meaning.

#### 3. Pictorial form against logical form — the discrimination the 2022 paper wants ✅

| Question | Pictorial form | Logical form |
|---|---|---|
| What is it? | what a picture must have in common with reality **to depict it at all in its medium** | the most abstract structural commonality — what **every** picture shares with reality |
| Example | a spatial model shares spatial form; a score shares acoustic form | every proposition shares logical form with the fact it depicts |
| Reach | limited to what shares that medium's form | unlimited: a proposition can depict **any** fact whatever |
| Status | a feature of a kind of picture | the form of **all possible representation** |
| Can it be depicted? | ✅ a spatial form can be represented in another medium | ⚠️ no — any depiction would presuppose it |

- ✅ **The second half of the question — how logical form defines the relation between language and reality.** Because logical form is common to proposition and fact, language and world are not two realms needing a bridge: they already share the structure that makes depiction possible. ✅ **2.18:** what a picture must have in common with reality in order to depict it at all is logical form. The relation is therefore **internal** — constitutive of the proposition — not an external correlation set up by convention or by causal contact.
- ⚠️ **And the price.** An internal relation cannot be described from outside. That is the transition to Session 11: the very thing that explains meaning turns out to be unsayable.

#### 4. What the picture theory rules out — stated before Session 10 develops it ✅

1. A proposition that depicts **no possible situation** is not false; it is **nonsensical (*unsinnig*)**.
2. A "proposition" that could not be false depicts no situation either; tautologies and contradictions are **senseless (*sinnlos*)** — well-formed but empty. (Session 10.)
3. Statements about the **relation between language and reality** attempt to depict the depicting relation itself, and fail. (Session 11.)
4. ⚠️ **None of this is the verification principle.** The *Tractatus* asks whether a proposition depicts a **possible fact**, not whether it can be **empirically checked**. The Vienna Circle's criterion is a later transformation of these resources and belongs to Topic 07.

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** The picture theory grounds meaning in shared structure rather than in reference or resemblance, and in doing so it makes falsity a normal case rather than a defect.
> **Named evidence.** The *Tractatus* opens by declaring that "the world is the totality of facts, not of things" (1.1) and that a fact is the existence of states of affairs, each a combination of objects (2, 2.01); a proposition is a logical picture whose elements are correlated with objects and whose arrangement depicts a possible arrangement of them, so that "in order to tell whether a picture is true or false we must compare it with reality" (2.223) and "it is impossible to tell from the picture alone whether it is true or false" (2.224).
> **Analysis.** Because what the picture shares with reality is form and not material, the theory explains how a sentence can be fully understood before its truth-value is known: understanding requires only that a possible configuration be presented, which is why *pictorial* form varies with the medium while *logical* form, being the form of representation as such, is shared by every picture and every fact.
> **Qualification.** The account is bought at the cost of two commitments the text never discharges — it supplies no uncontested example of a simple object or an elementary proposition, and it makes logical form itself indescribable, since any picture of it would already have to employ it — so the picture theory succeeds as an account of sense precisely by generating the say/show problem it ends with.

### SESSION 10 — BIPOLARITY, LOGICAL SPACE, THE GENERAL FORM OF THE PROPOSITION, AND THE TWO WAYS OF FAILING TO SAY ANYTHING

#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** For a sentence to say something, it has to be able to be true *and* able to be false. If it could not possibly be false, it is not telling you how things are — it is just spinning. Wittgenstein turns this into a whole system: every proposition marks out a place in the total space of possibilities, and every proposition whatever can be generated from a base of simplest propositions by one repeated logical operation. Sentences that fail this test fail in two different ways, and the difference between the two failures is examinable.

**Technical definition:** **Bipolarity** is the condition of sense: a proposition has **sense (*Sinn*)** only if it is capable of being true **and** capable of being false. **Logical space (*logischer Raum*)** is the totality of possible configurations; a proposition "determines a place in logical space" (**3.4**), so that understanding *p* is understanding what it excludes. The **general form of the proposition** (**6**) is ✅ **[ p̄ , ξ̄ , N(ξ̄) ]** — the rule generating every proposition from the totality of elementary propositions by repeated application of the **N-operator**, joint negation. Two failure modes follow: a **tautology** or **contradiction** is **senseless (*sinnlos*)** — well-formed, but saying nothing about the world; a metaphysical pseudo-proposition is **nonsensical (*unsinnig*)** — it depicts no possible situation at all.

#### ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING — WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM

> Wittgenstein's account of sense is a single condition worked out with unusual ruthlessness: a proposition says something only if the world could refute it — and once that is granted, logic's own truths turn out to say nothing, and metaphysics turns out not to be saying anything at all.

#### MUST-WRITE KEYWORDS

- **bipolarity** — capable of truth **and** capable of falsity; ⚠️ stronger than bivalence
- **sense (*Sinn*)** — what a proposition has when it presents a possible situation
- **logical space (*logischer Raum*)** — the totality of possibilities; a proposition determines a **place** in it
- **the fundamental idea (*Grundgedanke*)** — 4.0312, "the logical constants are not representatives"
- **the general form of the proposition** — 6, and the informal 4.5, "this is how things stand"
- **N-operator** — joint negation: none of these is true
- ***sinnlos*** against ***unsinnig*** — the two failures; the single most tested discrimination in the *Tractatus*

**How to use them:** treat bipolarity, logical space and the general form as **one doctrine seen from three sides**, and say so. That framing alone lifts an answer, because most scripts present them as three unrelated pieces of machinery.

#### 1. The two failure modes, side by side ✅

| Term | Status | Example | Cognitive value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tautology** — senseless (*sinnlos*) ✅ | true under every truth-condition; says nothing about the world | "It is raining or it is not raining" | logically valid but factually empty; ❌ **not** nonsensical |
| **Contradiction** — senseless (*sinnlos*) ✅ | false under every truth-condition | "It is raining and it is not raining" | a limiting case that says nothing |
| **Metaphysical pseudo-proposition** — nonsensical (*unsinnig*) ✅ | fails the conditions of factual sense altogether | "The Absolute is perfect"; "There are objects" | not a truth-functional picture of any possible fact |

- ✅ **Why tautologies are not nonsense.** They are perfectly well-formed and belong to the symbolism; they are the **limiting cases** of proposition-formation and they **show** the scaffolding of logic (4.461–4.4611). Wittgenstein's account of logical truth is thus that logic has no subject matter of its own.
- ⚠️ **Why the distinction is examinable.** The *sinnlos/unsinnig* pair is the single most frequently mishandled item in *Tractatus* answers, and it is also the point where scripts wrongly import the verification principle: the Vienna Circle's criterion tests for empirical checkability, whereas Wittgenstein's test is whether a possible situation is depicted at all.

#### 2. Elementary propositions and their independence — the assumption under pressure ⚠️❓

✅ **The commitment.** Elementary propositions consist of names in immediate combination and are **logically independent** of one another (2.061, 4.211): no elementary proposition follows from or excludes another, so every assignment of truth-values to them represents a possible configuration. This is stronger than ordinary bipolarity and it is what makes the truth-table method exhaustive.

❓ **The colour-exclusion problem.** "This patch is red all over" and "This patch is blue all over" are incompatible, yet neither looks like a truth-function of the other, and neither looks further analysable. If both are elementary, independence fails; if neither is, the text owes an analysis it does not supply.

⚠️ **How to state it safely.** The case **pressures** the independence assumption and helped drive Wittgenstein's 1929 "Some Remarks on Logical Form" — the only philosophical article besides the *Tractatus* published in his lifetime, and one whose proposed analysis he quickly abandoned. ❌ It does **not** by itself prove that no deeper analysis could preserve independence, and ❌ it must not be used as a licence to import meaning-as-use, which belongs to Topic 08.

#### 3. The four standing presuppositions of the whole apparatus ⚠️

1. **There are elementary propositions and simple objects** — although no uncontested example is given.
2. **Elementary propositions are logically independent** — which colour exclusion seriously pressures.
3. **All propositions are truth-functions of elementary ones** — while belief-contexts and modality create difficulties. (Wittgenstein's own treatment of "A believes that p" at 5.54–5.542 is itself contested.)
4. **The N-operator can handle infinite domains** — which remains disputed.

⚠️ **Write them as pressures and later developments, not as refutations conceded inside the text.** The *Tractatus* does not admit these as failures; it is later work, including Wittgenstein's own, that treats them as such.

#### 4. Why this session is the hinge of the whole *Tractatus* ✅

- ✅ **Backwards:** bipolarity is the picture theory stated as a *condition* rather than as a *model*. A picture that could not be false would not be presenting a situation at all.
- ✅ **Forwards:** the general form is simultaneously the rule that generates every proposition and the **criterion of the sayable**. Whatever the rule cannot produce is not a proposition — and that is exactly the boundary the Preface describes when it says that the limit can be drawn only *in language*, and that what lies on the other side will simply be nonsense.
- ⚠️ **The self-application problem is therefore built in.** Propositions 5 and 6 are not themselves truth-functions of elementary propositions. Session 11 takes up what Wittgenstein does about that.

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** Bipolarity, logical space and the general form of the proposition are not three doctrines but one: an account of sense as a determinate exclusion within a fixed field of possibilities.
> **Named evidence.** The *Tractatus* holds that a proposition can be true or false only by being a picture of reality (4.06) and that one cannot tell from the picture alone which it is (2.224); that a proposition determines a place in logical space (3.4) and is "like a solid body that restricts the freedom of movement of others" (4.463); that the logical constants are not representatives — Wittgenstein's own *fundamental idea* (4.0312); and that the general form of the proposition is [ p̄ , ξ̄ , N(ξ̄) ] (6), generated by repeated joint negation (5.502, 5.51).
> **Analysis.** Together these yield the two failure modes that any *Tractatus* answer must keep apart: a tautology or contradiction is *sinnlos*, well-formed but excluding nothing or everything, and therefore showing logic's scaffolding rather than describing the world, while a metaphysical sentence is *unsinnig* because it never entered logical space at all; and because logic needs no primitive propositions or logical objects, "there can be no surprises in logic" (6.1251).
> **Qualification.** The apparatus rests on four undischarged commitments — that there are simple objects and elementary propositions, that the latter are logically independent, that every proposition is truth-functional, and that the N-operator handles infinite domains — and colour exclusion pressures the second so directly that Wittgenstein revisited it in 1929, which is why the system is best presented as a rigorous programme with identifiable strain points rather than as a completed proof.

### SESSION 11 — SAYING AND SHOWING: THE LIMIT OF LANGUAGE, THE MYSTICAL, THE LADDER AND PROPOSITION 7

#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** Propositions tell us how things stand. But there is something a proposition cannot tell us: what makes it capable of telling us anything at all. Its logical form, the fact that it has that form, the existence of the objects it presupposes — these are not further facts to be reported; they display themselves in the proposition. Wittgenstein calls this the difference between what can be **said** and what can only be **shown**. Because ethics, aesthetics and the meaning of life are also not facts in the world, they too fall on the showing side — and so, embarrassingly, do the sentences of the *Tractatus* itself.

**Technical definition:** The **saying/showing distinction** separates what a proposition **states (*gesagt*)** — contingent states of affairs, the propositions of natural science — from what a proposition **displays (*gezeigt*)** — its own logical form, the logical properties of the world, the existence of objects presupposed by significant language, and, at the limit, value. ✅ *"What can be shown, cannot be said"* (**4.1212**). The distinction is **forced**, not stipulated: logical form is presupposed by every depiction, so any attempted depiction of it would already employ it. The *Tractatus* therefore closes with the **ladder** (**6.54**) — its own propositions are recognised as nonsensical by the reader who has used them to climb beyond them — and with **proposition 7**, which is uncommented and stands alone. ⚠️ There is **no proposition 7.1**.

#### ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING — WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM

> Wittgenstein's silence is not modesty, mysticism or reticence but the exact consequence of his own account of sense: since every proposition works by sharing logical form with a possible situation, the sharing itself can never be one more situation to be described — and what cannot be described cannot be said badly either, which is why the correct response is silence rather than caution.

#### MUST-WRITE KEYWORDS

- **said (*gesagt*) against shown (*gezeigt*)** — the distinction, in Wittgenstein's own vocabulary
- **4.1212** — "what can be shown, cannot be said"; safe verbatim
- **the limits of my language mean the limits of my world** — 5.6; the limit is drawn **from inside**
- **the mystical (*das Mystische*)** — 6.522: it shows itself; ⚠️ not "the emotional" or "the religious" loosely
- **the ladder** — 6.54, and the self-application problem it names
- **proposition 7** ⚠️ — quote it *and* name the translation; there is no 7.1
- **standard ineffability against resolute/therapeutic readings** ❓ — the interpretive dispute, stated in one clause

#### 1. The three things showing covers, kept apart ✅

1. **Logical form and logical properties.** That a proposition has the structure it has, that one proposition follows from another, that a tautology is a tautology — these show themselves in the symbolism. ✅ 6.124: the propositions of logic describe the scaffolding of the world, or rather they represent it.
2. **The existence of what significant language presupposes.** That there are objects, that the world has the general form it has — attempts to state these produce **nonsense (*unsinnig*)**, not falsehood. "There are objects" is Wittgenstein's own example of the failure.
3. **Value.** ✅ 6.41: the sense of the world must lie outside the world, for in the world everything is as it is and happens as it does happen, and in it there is no value. ✅ 6.42: there can be no propositions of ethics. ✅ 6.421: ethics cannot be put into words; ethics is transcendental. ✅ 6.522: "there is indeed the inexpressible; this **shows** itself; it is the mystical".

⚠️ **The verdict that must accompany the third.** The *Tractatus* does **not** say that ethical and religious claims are **false**, and it does not say they are unimportant. It says they are not **factual propositions**. ❌ Writing "Wittgenstein rejects ethics and religion as meaningless in the positivists' sense" fuses two different doctrines and is a marked error — the Vienna Circle drew an anti-metaphysical conclusion from a criterion Wittgenstein did not hold.

#### 2. Proposition 7 and the ladder — the exact wording discipline ✅

- ✅ **Ogden/Ramsey (1922):** *"Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent."*
- ✅ **Pears–McGuinness (1961):** *"What we cannot speak about we must pass over in silence."*
- ⚠️ **Name the translation whenever you quote 7.** Both are correct; presenting one as "the" wording is not. If unsure of any *Tractatus* wording, cite the **decimal number** instead — the numbering is identical in every edition and translation.
- ✅ **6.54, Pears–McGuinness:** *"My propositions serve as elucidations in the following way: anyone who understands me eventually recognises them as nonsensical, when he has used them — as steps — to climb beyond them. (He must, so to speak, throw away the ladder after he has climbed it.)"*
- ⚠️ **There is no proposition 7.1.** Proposition 7 is deliberately uncommented and stands alone; the decimal system means n.1 is a comment on n, and Wittgenstein supplies none. Writing "7.1" is a giveaway error.

#### 3. Is he justified? — the answer to the 2018 question, in five moves ⚠️

**The question asks** how the distinction points to "a single way of apprehending the most decisive problems of philosophy", and whether Wittgenstein is justified. The single way is this: **every decisive philosophical problem arises from an attempt to say what can only be shown.** Metaphysics tries to state the form of the world; epistemology tries to state the relation of thought to reality; ethics tries to state value. All three attempt to depict a condition of depiction.

1. ✅ **The strength.** The diagnosis is unified and it is *derived*, not asserted: it follows from the account of sense rather than being added to it. It also explains why philosophical problems feel intractable — they are not hard questions but malformed ones.
2. ✅ **The second strength.** It yields a genuinely new verdict on ethics. Ethical claims are not false, not confused and not unimportant; they are not in the business of stating facts at all. That is a more respectful conclusion than the positivists' later one.
3. ❓ **The self-application objection.** The distinction is itself stated in the *Tractatus*, in propositions that by its own test say nothing. If the book is nonsense, it cannot have established the boundary it draws.
4. ⚠️ **The two replies.** The **standard** reading treats 6.54 as an honest acknowledgment: the propositions are elucidations that bring the reader to a recognition which cannot be stated, and something genuinely manifests itself. The **resolute** reading denies that anything is left over: the sentences are plain nonsense, and the therapy consists in the reader's coming to see that he was never given a doctrine at all.
5. ⚠️ **The graded verdict.** Justified as a **diagnosis** — the reduction of a whole family of problems to one structural error is a real achievement, and the derivation is valid given the picture theory. Not fully justified as a **doctrine**, because the boundary cannot be stated without transgressing itself, and because the picture theory's own presuppositions (simples, independence, universal truth-functionality) are undischarged. ⚠️ The honest close is that the *Tractatus* succeeds precisely to the extent that it is read as an activity rather than as a body of theses — which is Wittgenstein's own description of philosophy at 4.112.

#### 4. Why silence is a *logical* consequence — the 2021 question in one paragraph ✅

⚠️ **The question ("Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent") is usually answered as if it expressed a mood.** It does not. The "must" is not prudential and not reverent. Given the account of sense, an attempt to speak beyond the sayable does not produce a *risky* or *imprecise* statement; it produces no statement. There is therefore nothing to be cautious about and nothing to be got wrong: the alternative to silence is not error but noise. ✅ 6.53 makes the pedagogic corollary explicit — the correct method in philosophy would be to say nothing except what can be said, and then, whenever someone tried to say something metaphysical, to demonstrate that he had failed to give a meaning to certain signs in his propositions.

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** The saying/showing distinction is forced on Wittgenstein by his own account of sense, which is why it delivers a unified diagnosis of philosophical problems and simultaneously undermines the book that states it.
> **Named evidence.** Since a proposition depicts only by sharing logical form with the situation it depicts, that sharing cannot itself be depicted — "what can be shown, cannot be said" (4.1212) — and the same applies to the existence of objects, to the logical truths that show the scaffolding of the world (6.124), and to value, since "the sense of the world must lie outside the world" (6.41), "there can be no propositions of ethics" (6.42) and "there is indeed the inexpressible; this shows itself; it is the mystical" (6.522).
> **Analysis.** The limit is therefore drawn from inside language — "the limits of my language mean the limits of my world" (5.6) — so the decisive problems of philosophy turn out to share one structure: each attempts to state a condition of stating, which is why silence at proposition 7 is a logical consequence rather than a counsel of prudence.
> **Qualification.** The cost is self-application: the *Tractatus*'s own propositions fail its test, and 6.54 concedes as much, so the standard ineffability reading and the resolute reading of Diamond and Conant divide over whether anything remains to be shown or whether the book is elucidatory nonsense throughout — a division a strong answer states before ruling that the work succeeds as a diagnosis and an activity rather than as a stateable doctrine.

### SESSION 12 — COMPARISONS, CRITICISMS AND REPLIES, ANSWER ARCHITECTURE, DIRECTIVES AND PROVENANCE

#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** This session is the craft session. It puts the three thinkers side by side so that comparative questions can be answered from a fixed grid rather than improvised; it collects the standard objections and the standard replies so that "critically discuss" has content; it gives the shape of a ten-, fifteen- and twenty-mark answer in this clause; and it fixes the dates, translations and attributions that a specialist examiner checks.

**Technical definition:** The **comparative and evaluative apparatus** of syllabus item 6 consists of (i) an axis-by-axis comparison of the three programmes; (ii) the specific contrast between **Russell's logical atomism** and the ***Tractatus*'s** atomism; (iii) the criticism-and-reply ledger for each thinker, with the **residual** left after each reply; (iv) the answer architectures for the three mark-values; (v) the **directive decoder** that converts a command word into a structural obligation; and (vi) the **translation, numbering and provenance discipline** required because Moore and Russell wrote in English and Wittgenstein did not.

#### ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING — WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM

> The three founders of analytic philosophy are best compared not by what they concluded but by what each was willing to leave unfinished: Moore leaves the analysis of ordinary knowledge open, Russell leaves the inventory of simples open, and the *Tractatus* leaves its own status open — and each of those three silences is exactly where the criticism lands.

#### MUST-WRITE KEYWORDS

- **axis first, then comparison** — the discipline that separates a comparison from two parallel descriptions
- **residual** — what survives after a reply; the word that signals a graded verdict
- **directive decoder** — matching the command word to the structural obligation
- **provenance discipline** — dates, translations and attributions, stated in a clause
- **owner boundary** — the sentence that keeps Topics 07, 08, 11 out of a Topic 06 answer

**How to use them:** in any "distinguish", "compare" or "do you find any difference" question, **name the axis before you compare on it**. Two parallel descriptions score as description; one axis with two positions on it scores as comparison.

#### 1. Answer architecture at three mark-values ✅

**10-mark — "The golden mountain is very high", 2025 Q1(d)**

```text
Problem : the sentence seems to be ABOUT a non-existent entity. Does it
          commit us to golden mountains? Is it meaningless?
Analysis: "the golden mountain" is an INCOMPLETE SYMBOL - no meaning in
          isolation. Analysed: there is exactly one golden mountain and
          it is very high - (Ex)[Gx & (Ay)(Gy -> y=x) & Hx].
Result  : the existence clause is false -> the whole statement is FALSE,
          not meaningless, and nothing need "subsist" (contra Meinong).
Point   : grammatical form != logical form; descriptions remove
          ontological inflation.
```

**15-mark — Moore's refutation of idealism with reference to blue/green/consciousness, 2025 Q3(c)**

```text
Frame   : the idealist claim - esse est percipi, to be is to be perceived.
Moore   : in every sensation distinguish (1) the ACT of awareness and
          (2) the OBJECT of awareness.
Quote   : "Blue is one object of sensation and green is another, and
          consciousness, which both sensations have in common, is
          different from either."
Key move: consciousness is DIAPHANOUS - we look THROUGH it to the object,
          which tempts us to conflate act and object. But they are
          distinct, and the comparison argument shows why.
Result  : object != act, so esse cannot be DEFINED as percipi; one
          idealist argument is blocked.
Assess  : Moore refutes an argument FOR idealism, not idealism; he does
          not prove unperceived existence, supplies no theory of
          perception, and does not touch Absolute Idealism. The act-object
          distinction nevertheless became foundational for analytic
          philosophy.
```

**20-mark — Russell's incomplete symbols leading to logical atomism, 2024 Q3(a)**

```text
Frame   : Russell's analytic method - reveal LOGICAL form behind
          GRAMMATICAL form.
Body-A  : INCOMPLETE SYMBOLS - no meaning in isolation; contextual
          definition; disappear on analysis. Theory of Descriptions:
          "The present King of France is bald" ->
          (Ex)[Kx & (Ay)(Ky -> y=x) & Bx]. Three puzzles solved:
          negative existentials, excluded middle (scope), substitutivity.
Body-B  : LOGICAL CONSTRUCTIONS - "substitute constructions out of known
          entities for inferences to unknown entities" (1914). Physical
          objects, nations, numbers, points.
Body-C  : LOGICAL ATOMISM - atomic facts <-> atomic propositions;
          molecular = truth-functions; isomorphism; "logical atoms and
          not physical atoms" (1918).
          The description theory REMOVES pseudo-constituents and
          SUPPORTS the search for genuine residues; it does NOT prove
          that analysis terminates or identify the atoms.
Assess  : strengths - Ockham's razor made operational; pseudo-problems
          dissolved. Weaknesses - the simples were never fixed; negative
          facts are a real cost; Strawson offers a rival analysis of
          descriptions; belief-contexts resist truth-functional
          treatment.
Close   : incomplete symbols are the scalpel of analytic philosophy;
          logical atomism is the anatomy toward which the scalpel cuts -
          and the anatomy was never completed.
```

| Sub-topic | **10-mark verdict** | **15-mark verdict** | **20-mark verdict** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Defence of common sense** | Moore changes the burden by claiming no sceptical premiss is more certain than the ordinary proposition denied | …the knowing/analysing distinction prevents conceptual difficulty from automatically defeating ordinary knowledge | the method weighs certainty but supplies no neutral proof of its premiss; the later hinge analysis is a relevant comparison, not owner content |
| **Proof of an external world** | the proof is valid and its premiss known, which is all a proof requires | …the question-begging objection is met dialectically rather than demonstratively | it reverses the burden without supplying a criterion of knowledge, and its deepest defence — framework certainty — comes from outside Moore |
| **Refutation of idealism** | Moore distinguishes awareness from its presented object, so *esse* cannot simply mean *percipi* | …transparency explains the temptation to conflate act and object, but introspective distinction alone may not establish mind-independence | the paper blocks one route to idealism and historically aids analytic realism; it neither refutes every idealism nor completes a theory of perception |
| **Theory of descriptions** | a description is contextually eliminated into existence, uniqueness and predication | …this handles empty descriptions, negative existentials and scope without a nonexistent denoted object | Strawson presses the account as natural-language pragmatics and presupposition; Russell's quantificational analysis remains powerful without being the only complete semantic account |
| **Acquaintance and description** | the distinction explains how discourse can concern items not directly presented | …the acquaintance principle motivates contextual analysis, but the theory also has independent logical payoffs | Russell's candidates for acquaintance and genuine names change across phases; Sellars and Kripke are bounded evaluation, and the logic outlives the epistemology |
| **Logical constructions** | contextual construction substitutes an analysed structure for an extra inferred entity | …physical-object construction is phase-specific and strained by possible sense-data | the technique establishes ontological economy; the full Carnap and Quine afterlives remain later ownership |
| **Logical atomism** | analysis seeks atomic facts and propositions, but description theory does not prove that a final base exists | …Russell identifies phase-specific particulars and universals; Wittgenstein postulates objects through combinatorial logical role | negative facts, unstable simples, colour incompatibility and non-extensional contexts pressure the two atomisms differently; do not treat them as one failed thesis |
| **Picture theory** | a proposition has sense by presenting a possible situation through shared logical form | …bipolarity, logical space and truth-functional generation form the programme | colour incompatibility and attitude and modal contexts pressure its elementary and extensional assumptions; later meaning-as-use must not be smuggled in |
| **Saying and showing** | logical form cannot be pictured as one more fact because every picture already presupposes it | …the ladder passage makes self-application deliberate rather than unnoticed | standard ineffability and resolute therapeutic readings disagree about what, if anything, remains as ineffable truth; a graded answer states both before ruling |

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** The comparative question in this clause is answered by fixing an axis, because the three programmes are alike in target and unlike in everything that follows from it.
> **Named evidence.** On the axis of what analysis reaches, Moore's 1925 distinction between knowing a proposition and knowing its analysis leaves the analysis of ordinary knowledge open; Russell's 1918 lectures seek "logical atoms and not physical atoms" as the last residue, having removed pseudo-constituents by the 1905 analysis of descriptions; and the *Tractatus* postulates simple objects because determinate sense requires them, while supplying no example of one.
> **Analysis.** The same axis therefore explains the criticisms: Moore is charged with begging the question because his terminal premiss is unanalysed, Russell with an unstable inventory because his residue is never exhibited, and Wittgenstein with self-refutation because the requirement for a base is itself stated in a proposition that fails his test.
> **Qualification.** The three failures are not the same failure, and treating them as one is the commonest way of losing the assessment mark: Moore's gap is epistemological, Russell's is ontological and Wittgenstein's is a problem about the status of philosophical discourse itself — which is why each of the three replies leaves a different residual.

*Concept spine: read it downward. One inherited target, three scalpels, one shared insight used three different ways, and three different endings.*

> 🔑 **Mnemonic — the ownership rule, "Moore DEFENDS, Russell DISSECTS, Wittgenstein PICTURES."** Nine of the ten commonest errors in this topic are attribution errors. Fix the owner before you write the doctrine.
> 🔑 **Mnemonic — Russell's descriptions in three beats, "E-U-P".** **E**xistence → **U**niqueness → **P**redication. Write the three conjuncts, then the scope point, then the puzzle solved.
> 🔑 **Mnemonic — Moore's proof in three tests, "D-K-F".** **D**ifferent premiss from conclusion → premiss **K**nown, not merely believed → conclusion **F**ollows.
> 🔑 **Mnemonic — the *Tractatus* ladder of sense, "B-L-G".** **B**ipolarity (the condition of sense) → **L**ogical space (where the possibilities live) → **G**eneral form of the proposition (the rule that generates all of them).
> 🔑 **Mnemonic — the two failure-words, "S before U".** ***Sinnlos*** = senseless but well-formed (tautology, contradiction). ***Unsinnig*** = nonsensical, no sense at all (metaphysical pseudo-proposition). Writing them as synonyms is a marked error.

canonical_block.block_text:
### ANSWER-WORTHINESS — WHAT EARNS MARKS AND WHAT DOES NOT

| Classification | Content |
|---|---|
| **CORE MAINS** | Moore's list of truisms and the knowing/analysing distinction (1925); the comparative-certainty method and the reversal of the burden of proof; the two-hands proof and Moore's own three conditions for a rigorous proof (1939); the awareness/object distinction and the transparency or diaphanous thesis, with the blue–green–consciousness sentence (1903); Russell's incomplete symbol and the contextual analysis of definite descriptions into existence, uniqueness and predication ("On Denoting", 1905); the three puzzles — negative existentials, excluded middle, substitutivity in attitude contexts; primary and secondary occurrence; the acquaintance/description distinction and the Principle of Acquaintance; logical constructions and the supreme maxim (1914); atomic and molecular propositions, atomic facts, the isomorphism thesis and negative facts (1918); "logical atoms, not physical atoms"; the *Tractatus* on facts rather than things (1.1), objects and states of affairs, the picture theory with pictorial form against logical form, bipolarity, logical space, the general form of the proposition at 6, *sinnlos* against *unsinnig*, saying against showing (4.1212), the ladder (6.54) and proposition 7 |
| **CORE SUPPORTING** | The provenance discipline: three different Moore papers of 1903, 1925 and 1939 with three different arguments; Russell's 1918 preface crediting the ideas to Wittgenstein; the German publication of 1921 and the bilingual *Tractatus* of 1922, with the Latin title suggested by Moore; the Ogden/Ramsey and Pears–McGuinness divergence at proposition 7 and at 4.5 and 6.54; *Sachverhalt* rendered "atomic fact" by Ogden and "state of affairs" by Pears–McGuinness; the fact that there is no proposition 7.1; the N-operator as joint negation; the phase-dependence of Russell's views, so that sense-data acquaintance, the 1918 atomism and later neutral monism are not one timeless doctrine; Strawson's presupposition objection (1950), Sellars on the Given (1956) and Kripke on rigid designation (lectures 1970, book 1980) as one-objection enrichment |
| **SUPPORTING** | Moore's paradox of analysis as method-context for why analysis is not trivial verbal substitution; the colour-exclusion problem of 1929 as a diagnosed internal pressure on the independence of elementary propositions; solipsism and the metaphysical subject at the limit of the world, kept to the depth the say/show boundary requires; the standard-ineffability against resolute/therapeutic dispute over 6.54, stated in one clause and then ruled on |
| **OPTIONAL ADVANCED** | Whether the theory of descriptions is a quantificational device or a deeper account of how apparent names disappear; whether logical constructions are genuine phenomenalist reductions or methodological housekeeping; what "showing" finally means, and whether the *Tractatus* self-destructs; Russell's paradox and the theory of types as the background technique behind "no meaning in isolation"; Moore's naturalistic fallacy named only to be excluded |
| **NOT OWNED HERE** | The verification principle and the rejection of metaphysics as a positive doctrine (Topic 07); meaning as use, language-games, family resemblance and the private-language argument (Topic 08); Strawson's own theory of reference and persons (Topic 11); Berkeley's immaterialism as doctrine (Topic 03); Hegel's Absolute Idealism as doctrine (Topic 05); Moore's ethics, including the naturalistic fallacy and the Open Question Argument; Russell's logicism, *Principia* technique and later neutral monism as systems |

⚠️ **Ownership boundary, stated once.** The printed clause names **three thinkers and seven doctrines**, and it is the only Western clause that makes attribution itself examinable. Everything in this package earns its place because a printed limb or one of the **fourteen** routed 2018–2025 question-parts requires it. Two consequences follow, and both are worth marks. First, no doctrine may be transferred between the three men: Moore's method is comparative certainty, Russell's is quantificational analysis, and early Wittgenstein's is a transcendental account of the conditions of representation, and a script that writes "Moore and Russell held that…" without a discriminating clause has already lost the attribution mark. Second, the topic ends where the *Tractatus* ends: the moment a script writes "and therefore only empirically verifiable statements are meaningful", it has answered Topic 07's question inside Topic 06's answer.

### ORIGIN AND CHRONOLOGY — THE MINIMUM NEEDED TO AVOID ANACHRONISM

⚠️ This clause is a **movement with a datable beginning**, and examiners test the dates through the papers rather than through biography. The rail below is the minimum that prevents the four commonest anachronisms: merging Moore's three papers, dating the English *Tractatus* to 1921, letting Russell's 1918 atomism absorb his later neutral monism, and importing the Vienna Circle into a Tractarian answer.

```text
   THE TARGET ALREADY IN PLACE
   1893  BRADLEY, Appearance and Reality - British Absolute Idealism at
         its height: internal relations, degrees of truth, the ordinary
         world demoted to "appearance"
        |
   THE REVOLT BEGINS - MOORE FIRST, RUSSELL FOLLOWING
   1903  MOORE, "The Refutation of Idealism" (Mind) ......... ACT/OBJECT
   1903  Moore, Principia Ethica - SAME YEAR, DIFFERENT SUBJECT.
         The naturalistic fallacy lives HERE, in ethics, not in item 6
   1905  RUSSELL, "On Denoting" (Mind) .............. DESCRIPTIONS BEGIN
         Ramsey later calls it "a paradigm of philosophy"
   1910-11 Russell, "Knowledge by Acquaintance and Knowledge by
         Description" (Proceedings of the Aristotelian Society)
   1910-13 Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica - the technique
         of CONTEXTUAL DEFINITION that "incomplete symbol" names
   1912  Russell, The Problems of Philosophy, Ch. 5 - the PRINCIPLE OF
         ACQUAINTANCE, safe to quote verbatim
   1914  Russell, Our Knowledge of the External World + "The Relation of
         Sense-Data to Physics" .................. LOGICAL CONSTRUCTIONS
        |
   THE TWO ATOMISMS, WRITTEN IN THE SAME YEARS
   1918  RUSSELL, "The Philosophy of Logical Atomism" - lectures given in
         London, published in The Monist 1918-19. Russell's own preface
         credits the ideas to Wittgenstein. SAY SO IN THE EXAM.
   1918  WITTGENSTEIN completes the Tractatus manuscript while on active
         service and then in captivity
   1921  German text published as Logisch-Philosophische Abhandlung in
         Annalen der Naturphilosophie
   1922  BILINGUAL EDITION, German-English, with the Latin title
         Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus - the title was MOORE'S
         SUGGESTION. Ogden translation, assisted by Ramsey, checked by
         Wittgenstein. NEVER date the English text 1921.
        |
   MOORE COMPLETES HIS CASE
   1925  MOORE, "A Defence of Common Sense" (Contemporary British
         Philosophy) ................................. THE TRUISMS PAPER
   1939  MOORE, "Proof of an External World" (British Academy lecture)
         ................................................. THE HANDS PAPER
        |
   THE PRESSURES THAT END THE PERIOD
   1929  Wittgenstein, "Some Remarks on Logical Form" (PAS Supplementary)
         - the COLOUR-EXCLUSION problem; the only philosophical article
         besides the Tractatus published in his lifetime, and an analysis
         he quickly abandoned
   1929+ VIENNA CIRCLE takes Tractarian resources in a direction
         Wittgenstein did not take them ................... TOPIC 07
   1950  STRAWSON, "On Referring" (Mind) - presupposition, not falsity
   1953  Philosophical Investigations, posthumous ......... TOPIC 08
   1956  SELLARS, "Empiricism and the Philosophy of Mind" - the Myth of
         the Given, against acquaintance as bedrock
   1961  PEARS-McGUINNESS translation of the Tractatus - divergent
         wording at exactly the most quoted propositions
   1970/1980 KRIPKE, Naming and Necessity - lectures 1970, book 1980;
         give ONE date, not a merged one
```

⚠️ **What the rail earns you.** Three separate marks are commonly available from it: the 1903/1925/1939 separation in any Moore answer; Russell's own 1918 attribution of atomism to Wittgenstein in any atomism answer; and the 1921/1922 distinction in any *Tractatus* answer. None of them costs more than a clause.

canonical_block.source_heading: SESSION 1 — THE ANALYTIC REVOLT: THREE PROGRAMMES, ONE TARGET, AND THE ATTRIBUTION FIREWALL
canonical_block.block_text:
### SESSION 1 — THE ANALYTIC REVOLT: THREE PROGRAMMES, ONE TARGET, AND THE ATTRIBUTION FIREWALL

#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** At the turn of the twentieth century three Cambridge philosophers stopped trying to build a picture of reality as a whole and started examining, one at a time, the individual sentences in which philosophical claims are made. They asked what a sentence commits you to, what its real structure is, and whether it succeeds in saying anything at all. That change of unit — from *system* to *proposition* — is what is meant by the analytic revolt.

**Technical definition:** **Analytic philosophy**, in its founding phase, is the programme of settling philosophical questions by the **analysis of propositions** rather than by the construction of a metaphysical system. Its shared negative target is **British Absolute Idealism** — the monistic doctrine, associated with F. H. Bradley and J. M. E. McTaggart and inherited ultimately from Hegel, that relations are internal, that ordinary things and ordinary judgements are "appearance", and that only the whole is fully real. Its shared positive commitment is that **grammatical form need not be logical form**. ⚠️ Beyond that shared commitment the three programmes diverge completely in method, in what analysis is supposed to reach, and in what counts as success.

#### ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING — WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM

> The founders of analytic philosophy were united by what they refused rather than by what they proposed: Moore, Russell and the early Wittgenstein all denied that a philosophical system may overrule what we ordinarily know or ordinarily say, and each then built a completely different instrument for showing why — comparative certainty, quantificational analysis, and a transcendental account of the conditions of sense.

#### MUST-WRITE KEYWORDS

- **analysis** — the shared method, and the term whose three different senses this clause turns on
- **British Absolute Idealism** — the named target, not "idealism" in general
- **grammatical form is not logical form** — the single shared insight of Russell and the *Tractatus*
- **act/object distinction** — Moore's instrument, taken over by Russell for sense-data
- **atomic fact / state of affairs (*Sachverhalt*)** — the two atomisms, deliberately kept apart
- **attribution firewall** — the discipline of never letting one man's doctrine drift onto another

**How to use them:** name the target in your first clause, because "revolt" without a named opponent reads as decoration; then state the shared insight; then immediately divide the three programmes, because the division is the marks-bearing content of any comparative question in this clause.

   |  certain than |  |  was never a name. |  | "Your sentence never |

#### 1. What exactly was being revolted against

✅ British Absolute Idealism held that reality is a single spiritual whole; that relations are **internal**, so that nothing could be what it is if its relations were different; and that ordinary claims about separate things in space and time are therefore true only in a degraded sense — "appearance", in Bradley's word, arranged by **degrees of truth**.

⚠️ The consequence that provoked the revolt is a methodological one. If ordinary claims are appearance, then a sufficiently powerful system may correct them wholesale. Moore's answer is that this gets the order of confidence backwards; Russell's is that the doctrine of internal relations is an artefact of taking every proposition to have subject–predicate form; Wittgenstein's is that the system's own sentences fail the test any sentence must pass to have sense.

⚠️ **What not to overwrite.** Hegel's Absolute Idealism is Topic 05 and Berkeley's immaterialism is Topic 03. This session needs the target only as a target. ❌ It is a marked error to answer "Moore's refutation of idealism" by expounding Hegel, and ❌ equally an error to treat Bradley's monism and Berkeley's *esse est percipi* as the same doctrine — Moore's 1903 paper attacks the second, not the first.

#### 2. Three senses of "analysis" — the distinction that most scripts miss

| Programme | What analysis takes as input | What it delivers | When it has succeeded |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Moore** ✅ | an ordinary judgement we already know to be true | an account of what that judgement commits us to | when the commitments are clear; ⚠️ and if they are not, the *knowledge* is untouched |
| **Russell** ✅ | a sentence whose surface suggests a suspect entity | a quantified paraphrase in which the apparent name disappears | when the paraphrase preserves truth-conditions and removes the ontological commitment |
| **Early Wittgenstein** ✅ | any proposition whatever | its resolution into truth-functions of elementary propositions | when the analysis reaches a base of logically independent elementary propositions — ⚠️ a base the *Tractatus* requires but never exhibits |

- ⚠️ **The examinable consequence.** Because "analysis" means three different things, the three men can share a slogan and still disagree about everything that matters. Russell's descriptions do not vindicate Moore's truisms; Moore never accepted that ordinary objects are constructions; Wittgenstein's objects are not Russell's sense-data.

#### 3. Where influence really ran — and why the direction is worth a mark

✅ Russell's 1918 lectures open by disclaiming originality: he presents logical atomism as growing out of conversations with Wittgenstein, his student from 1911. ⚠️ Writing "Russell invented logical atomism and Wittgenstein developed it" is therefore doubly wrong — it reverses the credit Russell himself gave, and it suggests a single doctrine where there are two.

✅ In the other direction the debts are equally concrete: Wittgenstein takes the technique of the **variable and the quantifier** from Russell and Frege, and then removes what he regards as their central mistake — the treatment of logical constants as names of anything (4.0312, the *fundamental idea* or *Grundgedanke*). ✅ Moore's contribution is earlier and different in kind: the **act/object distinction** of 1903, which Russell adopts wholesale for sense-data, and the tone of the whole movement — the refusal to be argued out of what one knows.

#### 4. What each programme finally achieved, stated without inflation

1. **Moore** ✅ reversed the burden of proof in epistemology and made ordinary knowledge a fixed point against which theories are tested. ⚠️ He did not supply a neutral criterion for deciding whose premisses are more certain, and the objection that his proof begs the question against the sceptic is not silenced.
2. **Russell** ✅ produced in the theory of descriptions a technique still in universal use, and with it a general method of ontological economy. ⚠️ He never fixed the final inventory of simples, admitted negative facts as a cost, and changed his own view of the base more than once.
3. **Early Wittgenstein** ✅ gave the most complete account ever attempted of the conditions under which a sentence has sense, and drew from it a boundary around the sayable. ⚠️ The account's own statement falls outside that boundary, which is the ladder problem of 6.54 — a difficulty the book itself raises rather than one imported by critics.

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** The early analytic movement is best characterised negatively: what unites Moore, Russell and the early Wittgenstein is a refusal to let a philosophical system overrule ordinary knowledge or ordinary discourse, not a shared positive doctrine.
> **Named evidence.** Moore's "The Refutation of Idealism" (1903) and "A Defence of Common Sense" (1925) protect ordinary certainties by comparing them with sceptical premisses; Russell's "On Denoting" (1905) rewrites "the F is G" as an existentially quantified sentence so that the apparent name disappears; the *Tractatus* (1921/1922) grounds sense in shared logical form and consigns what cannot be depicted to the domain of what can only be shown.
> **Analysis.** Each instrument works on the proposition rather than on the system, which is why the shared insight is formal — that grammatical form may misdescribe logical form — and why the shared enemy is a monism that had made ordinary judgement provisional.
> **Qualification.** The unity is genuine but thin: "analysis" names commitment-clarification in Moore, quantificational paraphrase in Russell and the resolution of propositions into a truth-functional base in Wittgenstein, so a script that treats the three as one programme has recorded the movement's slogan while missing its content.

#### Exam link

- **2018 Q4(c)** and **2024 Q3(a)** both ask how a Russellian technique *leads to* atomism; §2 supplies the discrimination that keeps the answer from sliding into Wittgenstein's atomism.
- **2018 Q3(a)** (Empiricism-owned) explicitly asks whether Moore's reaction to Berkeley differs from Russell's; §2 and §3 are the whole answer to the comparative half.
- **2022 Q1(b)** ("Russell's method of logical analysis") is opened correctly by the third column of §2 and closed by §4.2.

#### UPSC traps

| Trap | Correction |
|---|---|
| "Moore, Russell and Wittgenstein held the same view" | They shared a target and an insight about form. Their methods, their ontologies and their criteria of success differ |
| Treating the target as Hegel or Berkeley indifferently | The movement's local opponent is **British Absolute Idealism**; Moore's 1903 paper attacks *esse est percipi* specifically |
| "Russell invented logical atomism" | His own 1918 preface credits the ideas to Wittgenstein — and the two atomisms are still not identical |
| Importing the naturalistic fallacy into this clause | It belongs to *Principia Ethica* (1903) and to ethics. Same author, same year, different syllabus item |
| Ending the topic with verificationism | The *Tractatus* asks whether a sentence depicts a possible situation, not whether it can be empirically checked |

#### Revision notes

- Target: British Absolute Idealism — internal relations, degrees of truth, ordinary world as appearance (Bradley, McTaggart).
- Shared insight: grammatical form is not logical form. Shared unit: the proposition.
- Three analyses: commitment (Moore) · quantificational paraphrase (Russell) · resolution into a truth-functional base (Wittgenstein).
- Ownership: Moore owns commonsense and refutation of idealism; Russell owns atomism, constructions, incomplete symbols; Wittgenstein owns picture theory and saying/showing; atomism is jointly listed and doubly meant.
- Dates for the mark: 1903 Moore · 1905 "On Denoting" · 1914 constructions · 1918 both atomisms · 1921 German, 1922 bilingual · 1925 truisms · 1939 hands.
- Achievements with their costs: burden reversed without a neutral criterion · economy without a fixed inventory · a boundary of sense that its own statement crosses.

```text
BRITISH ABSOLUTE IDEALISM (internal relations, appearance, degrees of truth)
        |
        v
ONE NEGATIVE THESIS: no system may overrule what we ordinarily know or say

        +--> MOORE 1903/1925/1939  compare CERTAINTIES; act != object
        +--> RUSSELL 1905/1914/1918  rewrite LOGICAL FORM; economise ontology
        +--> WITTGENSTEIN 1918/1921/1922  fix the CONDITIONS OF SENSE
        |
        v
SHARED INSIGHT: GRAMMATICAL FORM != LOGICAL FORM
SHARED UNIT:    the PROPOSITION, not the system
        |
        v
ATTRIBUTION FIREWALL: seven printed terms, three owners, one jointly listed
NOT HERE: naturalistic fallacy | verification | meaning-as-use | Strawson's
   positive semantics
        |
        v
ANSWER LINE: they agree that philosophy proceeds by analysis and disagree
   about what analysis reaches
```

canonical_block.block_text:
#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** At the turn of the twentieth century three Cambridge philosophers stopped trying to build a picture of reality as a whole and started examining, one at a time, the individual sentences in which philosophical claims are made. They asked what a sentence commits you to, what its real structure is, and whether it succeeds in saying anything at all. That change of unit — from *system* to *proposition* — is what is meant by the analytic revolt.

**Technical definition:** **Analytic philosophy**, in its founding phase, is the programme of settling philosophical questions by the **analysis of propositions** rather than by the construction of a metaphysical system. Its shared negative target is **British Absolute Idealism** — the monistic doctrine, associated with F. H. Bradley and J. M. E. McTaggart and inherited ultimately from Hegel, that relations are internal, that ordinary things and ordinary judgements are "appearance", and that only the whole is fully real. Its shared positive commitment is that **grammatical form need not be logical form**. ⚠️ Beyond that shared commitment the three programmes diverge completely in method, in what analysis is supposed to reach, and in what counts as success.

3. **Early Wittgenstein** ✅ gave the most complete account ever attempted of the conditions under which a sentence has sense, and drew from it a boundary around the sayable. ⚠️ The account's own statement falls outside that boundary, which is the ladder problem of 6.54 — a difficulty the book itself raises rather than one imported by critics.

canonical_block.block_text:
#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** The early analytic movement is best characterised negatively: what unites Moore, Russell and the early Wittgenstein is a refusal to let a philosophical system overrule ordinary knowledge or ordinary discourse, not a shared positive doctrine.
> **Named evidence.** Moore's "The Refutation of Idealism" (1903) and "A Defence of Common Sense" (1925) protect ordinary certainties by comparing them with sceptical premisses; Russell's "On Denoting" (1905) rewrites "the F is G" as an existentially quantified sentence so that the apparent name disappears; the *Tractatus* (1921/1922) grounds sense in shared logical form and consigns what cannot be depicted to the domain of what can only be shown.
> **Analysis.** Each instrument works on the proposition rather than on the system, which is why the shared insight is formal — that grammatical form may misdescribe logical form — and why the shared enemy is a monism that had made ordinary judgement provisional.
> **Qualification.** The unity is genuine but thin: "analysis" names commitment-clarification in Moore, quantificational paraphrase in Russell and the resolution of propositions into a truth-functional base in Wittgenstein, so a script that treats the three as one programme has recorded the movement's slogan while missing its content.

canonical_block.block_text:
### SESSION 2 — MOORE'S DEFENCE OF COMMON SENSE: TRUISMS, KNOWING AGAINST ANALYSING, AND COMPARATIVE CERTAINTY

#### DEFINITION / WHAT THIS IS CALLED

**Plain-language definition:** Moore says there is a set of very ordinary claims — that the earth existed for many years before he was born, that he has a body, that there are other people with bodies — which he *knows*, with certainty, to be true. Any philosophical argument that ends by denying one of them must contain a premiss he is less sure of than he is of the claim being denied; so the rational response is to reject the argument, not the claim.

**Technical definition:** Moore's **defence of common sense** ("A Defence of Common Sense", 1925) consists of (i) a list of ordinary propositions — his **truisms** — which he asserts he knows with certainty and which he claims are known by very many others; (ii) the distinction between **knowing that a proposition is true** and **knowing its correct analysis**; and (iii) a **comparative-certainty** principle: a philosophical argument overturns a truism only if every premiss of the argument is more certain than the truism, and no sceptical or idealist premiss has ever met that condition. ⚠️ "Common sense" here is not opinion-polling, convention or majority belief; the list is philosophically contestable rather than infallible by definition.

#### ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING — WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM

> Moore's defence of common sense is not the claim that ordinary belief is beyond criticism but the far narrower and far more effective claim that no philosopher has ever produced a premiss more certain than "I have a body" — so that when a system and a truism collide, it is the system whose credentials must be re-examined first.

#### MUST-WRITE KEYWORDS

- **truisms** — Moore's own word for the propositions on the list
- **knowing that P against knowing the analysis of P** — the distinction that does the defensive work
- **comparative certainty** — the method: weigh the premiss against the proposition it would overturn
- **reversal of the burden of proof** — the result, stated in the examiner's language
- **common-sense realism** — the label the 2019 paper uses; explain *why* it is applied
- ⚠️ **not a popularity claim** — say this explicitly; it pre-empts the commonest objection

**How to use them:** never open a Moore answer with the hands. Open with the *structure* — a list, a distinction and a comparison — because the 2019, 2021 and 2024 questions all ask for arguments, and the hands are a separate paper of 1939 answering a separate question.

#### Plain-language visual — the weighing scale

```text
   THE SCEPTIC'S ARGUMENT              MOORE'S TRUISM
   +---------------------------+       +---------------------------+
   | P1  I cannot rule out     |       |  I have a body.           |
   |     that I am dreaming.   |       |                           |
   | P2  If I cannot rule that |  vs   |  The earth existed for    |
   |     out, I do not know    |       |  many years before I was  |
   |     I have a body.        |       |  born.                    |
   | C   So I do not know I    |       |                           |
   |     have a body.          |       |  There are other human    |
   +---------------------------+       |  beings, with bodies.     |
                                       +---------------------------+
              HOW CERTAIN                        HOW CERTAIN
              ARE P1 AND P2?                     IS THE TRUISM?
                   |                                   |
                  v                                  v
        abstract, technical,                 as certain as anything
        contested by competent               I have ever been
        philosophers
                   |                                   |
                   +----------------> WEIGH <----------+
                                        |
                                        v
                   THE ARGUMENT IS VALID, SO ONE OF THREE THINGS
                   MUST GO. MOORE: GIVE UP A PREMISS, NOT THE
                   CONCLUSION YOU WERE MOST SURE OF.
```

**In simple words:** a valid argument is a set of scales, not a one-way street. If the conclusion is something you are more certain is false than you are certain any premiss is true, then the argument has not proved its conclusion — it has *refuted one of its own premisses*. Moore's contribution is to insist that we actually perform the weighing instead of assuming that the philosophical premiss automatically wins because it is philosophical.

| Remember first | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Truisms are **known**, not merely believed | Moore's claim is epistemic, and he insists on the word "know" |
| Knowing is not analysing | difficulty about what "material object" *means* leaves the knowledge standing |
| The method is **comparative** | it never claims the truism is self-evidently unassailable, only that it outweighs its rivals |
| The list is **contestable** | Moore offers it as what he knows, not as a definition of truth |
| The result is **dialectical** | the sceptic now owes an account of why abstract premisses beat perceptual ones |

> **One-line memory:** the argument is valid — so which end of it do you trust more?

#### 🖼️ VISUAL — the structure of the 1925 defence

```text
   STEP 1  THE LIST OF TRUISMS (Moore's own examples)
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   | "There exists at present a living human body, which is my      |
   |  body."                                                        |
   | "This body has existed continuously on or near the earth."     |
   | "The earth has existed for many years past."                   |
   | "There have existed many other human beings, with bodies."     |
   | "I am a human being who has had many experiences."             |
   | AND: very many other human beings know propositions of the     |
   |  same kind about themselves.                                   |
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
   STEP 2  THE LEVEL DISTINCTION - the load-bearing move
   +--------------------------------+------------------------------+
   | KNOWING THAT P IS TRUE         | KNOWING THE ANALYSIS OF P    |
   | certain: "I have two hands"    | doubtful: what IS a material |
   |                                | object? sense-data? a class  |
   | pre-philosophical, secure      | of appearances? a substance? |
   |                                | PHILOSOPHICAL WORK PROPER,   |
   |                                | and it may remain unfinished |
   +--------------------------------+------------------------------+
   THE FALLACY MOORE NAMES: "you cannot know you have hands because
   you cannot analyse 'material object'" CONFUSES THE TWO LEVELS.
                              |
   STEP 3  THE COMPARATIVE-CERTAINTY PRINCIPLE
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   | For a philosophical argument to overturn a truism, EVERY       |
   | premiss must be MORE certain than the truism it denies.        |
   | Moore's empirical claim: no such premiss has been produced.    |
   | Therefore the rational move is to reject a premiss.            |
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
   STEP 4  THE RESULT, IN THE EXAMINER'S WORDS
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   | THE BURDEN OF PROOF IS REVERSED. The realist no longer owes a  |
   | proof of the external world from neutral ground; the sceptic   |
   | owes an explanation of why his abstract premisses should be    |
   | trusted more than an ordinary perceptual certainty.            |
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
   THE LIMIT THAT MUST BE WRITTEN
   ⚠️ The principle presupposes that certainty is COMPARABLE across
   ordinary and philosophical propositions, and Moore supplies NO
   NEUTRAL MEASURE for the comparison. A sceptic who simply denies
   that Moore knows the truism has not been shown to be irrational -
   he has been told that Moore is more confident.
```

⚠️ **Caption.** Steps 1–3 are what the 2021 and 2024 questions call "the arguments". Step 4 is the verdict. The bottom band is the assessment half, and the questions in 2021 and 2024 both explicitly demand it.

#### 1. Why the list matters as a list

✅ Moore does not argue *for* the truisms from something more basic — that would concede that they need support from outside. He **asserts** them, and asserts in addition that he knows them, and that others know propositions of the same kind. The list is therefore doing two jobs at once: it fixes what is to be defended, and it displays how enormous the sceptic's task is, since the sceptic must deny not one claim but a whole interlocking body of them.

⚠️ **The second-order claim is the more interesting one.** Moore also claims to know that *other people know* such propositions. This matters because it converts the defence from a report of personal confidence into a claim about a shared epistemic position, and because it is what makes "common sense" the right name — the propositions are common to us, not merely evident to Moore.

❌ **What the doctrine is not.** It is not the claim that whatever most people believe is true; it is not an appeal to convention; and it is not a claim of infallibility. Moore's own list is a philosophical proposal and can be argued with. State this in one clause and the commonest objection is disarmed before it is raised.

#### 2. The knowing/analysing distinction, and the confusion of levels it exposes

| The sceptical or idealist move | Moore's diagnosis |
|---|---|
| "The analysis of 'material object' is disputed, therefore we do not know that material objects exist" ✅ | A **confusion of levels**: the truth of a proposition and the correct account of its constituents are different questions, established by different means |
| "Since sense-data are all we are directly given, ordinary claims are at best inferences" ⚠️ | Moore accepts a real question about how truisms relate to sense-data; he denies that leaving it open suspends the knowledge |
| "Ordinary language is loose, so ordinary claims are imprecise" ⚠️ | Imprecision in stating a proposition is not doubt about it; Moore's certainty attaches to the proposition, not to a formulation |

- ✅ **Why this is the load-bearing move.** Without it, the defence would be a bare refusal to engage. With it, Moore can concede the entire difficulty of philosophical analysis — he was himself a lifelong analyst, and the paradox of analysis is *his* problem — while denying that the difficulty reaches the knowledge.
- ⚠️ **The honest cost.** The distinction protects the knowledge only if propositional knowledge really can be secure while its constituents are unclear. That is exactly what a sceptic about the given, or a philosopher who ties understanding to analysis, will deny.

#### 3. The paradox of analysis — the difficulty Moore's own method creates ⚠️

If the correct analysis of "X is a brother" is "X is a male sibling", then either the analysis says the very same thing as the original, in which case it is trivially uninformative; or it says something different, in which case it is not an analysis of that concept at all.

- ⚠️ The paradox is associated with Moore and has **no settled Moorean solution**. Fregean differences of sense or mode of presentation, and later accounts of concept-possession and synonymy, are proposed responses rather than agreed ones.
- ⚠️ **Owner scope.** This is **method-context, not a printed limb**. Use it for one purpose only: to show why analysis cannot be reduced to trivial verbal substitution, and therefore why Moore needed the knowing/analysing distinction in the first place. Do not build a section of an answer on it.

#### 4. Why the label "common-sense realism" is applied — the 2019 question in one paragraph

✅ **Common sense**, because the defended propositions are the ordinary ones and the method is comparison with them rather than derivation from a philosophical first principle. ✅ **Realism**, because the truisms include the existence of a body, of the earth before one's birth and of other human beings — that is, of things whose existence does not consist in being perceived by the person asserting them. ⚠️ **The qualification that earns the assessment mark:** the realism is a *consequence* of defending the truisms, not an independently argued metaphysics. Moore gives no theory of perception, does not settle whether ordinary objects are analysable into sense-data, and offers no account of the relation between the two levels. His realism is the position he ends in, not the premiss he starts from.

#### HOW TO WRITE THE PARAGRAPH — claim → named evidence → analysis → qualification

> **Claim.** Moore's defence of common sense succeeds as a redistribution of dialectical burden and fails, by design, as a demonstration that scepticism is false.
> **Named evidence.** "A Defence of Common Sense" (1925) lists truisms — that he has a body, that the earth existed for many years before his birth, that there are other human beings with bodies — asserts that he knows them, distinguishes knowing a proposition from knowing its analysis, and rests the defence on the comparison of certainties.
> **Analysis.** Because a valid argument transmits certainty backwards as well as forwards, an argument whose conclusion is less credible than its own premisses are is one that has refuted a premiss; Moore's contribution is to insist that the comparison actually be made, and to point out that no sceptical premiss has ever been more evident than "I have a body".
> **Qualification.** The method presupposes that certainty can be compared across ordinary and philosophical propositions without a neutral measure, so a sceptic who simply denies that Moore *knows* the truism has not been refuted but only outweighed — which is why Moore's own verdict is that scepticism has not been shown to be true rather than that it has been shown to be false.

#### Exam link

- **2019 Q3(c)** ("Why is Moore's philosophy called common-sense realism?") is answered by §4, with §1–§2 as the supporting structure. The question asks *why the label is applied*, so the answer must justify both words.
- **2024 Q1(c)** ("What arguments are offered by Moore to prove that there are certain truisms…? Critically discuss.") takes §1–§3 for the arguments and the bottom band of the visual for the "critically".
- **2021 Q3(a)**, twenty marks, adds the explicit sceptical half; that question is completed in Session 3.

#### UPSC traps

| Trap | Correction |
|---|---|
| Answering the 1925 question with the 1939 hands | Different paper, different argument. The truisms paper contains no proof; the proof paper is a separate lecture |
| "Common sense means what most people believe" | It means a specific list of ordinary propositions Moore claims to know; popularity plays no role in the argument |
| Presenting the truisms as self-evident axioms | Moore claims to *know* them, not that they are indubitable by definition; the list is philosophically contestable |
| Omitting the knowing/analysing distinction | Without it the defence looks like a refusal to argue, and the answer loses its central move |
| Claiming Moore refutes scepticism | He shifts the burden. His own conclusion is that no sceptical premiss has been shown more certain than the truism it denies |

#### Revision notes

- 1925 "A Defence of Common Sense": list of truisms + second-order claim that others know propositions of the same kind.
- Knowing that P is not knowing the analysis of P; the sceptic's inference from analytic difficulty to ignorance is a confusion of levels.
- Comparative certainty: an argument overturns a truism only if every premiss is more certain than the truism.
- Result: reversal of the burden of proof; ⚠️ no neutral measure of certainty is supplied.
- ❌ Not popularity, not convention, not infallibility.
- Paradox of analysis: bounded method-context, no settled Moorean solution, explains why analysis is not verbal substitution.
- "Common-sense realism": common sense from the method, realism from the content of the list; the realism is a result, not a premiss.

#### CLOSING RECALL FLOW — THE DEFENCE OF COMMON SENSE

```text
1925 "A DEFENCE OF COMMON SENSE"
        |
        +--> LIST OF TRUISMS (my body | the earth before my birth |
        |    other human beings with bodies) + others know the same kind
        |
        +--> LEVEL DISTINCTION: knowing that P  !=  knowing P's ANALYSIS
        |    so analytic difficulty does NOT cancel knowledge
        |
        +--> COMPARATIVE CERTAINTY: every premiss must outweigh the
             truism it denies - and none ever has
        |
        v
RESULT: THE BURDEN OF PROOF IS REVERSED
        |
        v
LIMIT (write it): no NEUTRAL measure of certainty is supplied; the
   sceptic is outweighed, not shown to be irrational
        |
        v
LABEL: COMMON-SENSE (method) + REALISM (content of the list), and the
   realism is a RESULT, not an independently argued metaphysics
ANSWER LINE: no philosopher has produced a premiss more certain than
   "I have a body"
```
